briefs.source_chain: Mixed Iran headlines leave oil only modestly higher, so hawkish Fedspeak (Cook, Barkin) plus a hot Dallas Fed print drive a bond selloff to a 19-year yield high, which drags equities down (tech lags ex-NVDA on its buyback; META's Enterprise Platform launch/MDB-CEO hire drags related software and CPU names) -> JPM flips back to Tactically Bullish from its Aug 31 Cautious/Neutral call on expected yield stabilization and lower oil, dropping the +NDX/-RTY pair for Tech outright plus Banks ex-AI, and previews JOLTS/MU.
briefs.brief_chain: Same structure: mixed Iran headlines -> oil only modestly higher -> bond selloff/yields to 19-year high on hawkish Fedspeak + hot Dallas Fed -> SPX down, tech lags ex-NVDA -> META drop drags enterprise software/CPU names -> JPM flips Tactically Bullish, drops NDX/RTY pair for Tech + Banks ex-AI, previews JOLTS/MU.

distortions.what: Brief states NVDA +1.3%. The source itself carries two different NVDA figures in different sections (1.7% in the Afternoon Updates line, 1.3% in the Trading Desk Commentary line); the brief silently picks one without flagging the internal inconsistency.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — both figures are positive and close in magnitude; the buyback-driven bullish read on NVDA is unchanged either way.

distortions.what: Brief attributes both 'profit-taking and de-risking' broadly to the dragged-down enterprise software AND CPU names, while the source specifically ties profit-taking to META and de-risking to infra software (long-onlys), not explicitly to the CPU-names group.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the directional read (bearish pressure on these groups) is unchanged; only the mechanism attribution is compressed.

briefs.source_chain: A midday Iran sanctions-relief headline is quickly rebutted -> oil/rates rise, driving a risk-off tape with breadth at dot-com-era lows and SPX through 'negative forward returns' technical levels -> AI/tech takes added pressure from OpenAI's training pause, Musk's Muse privacy comments and MDB's CEO departure, partly offset by NVDA's buyback boost and new safety platform -> desk finishes a net seller (asset managers and hedge funds both better for sale) -> GS's model projects heavy CTA RTY-futures selling next week, while dealers stay long S&P gamma but flip short NDX above +4%.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: Iran headline reversal -> oil/rates up, risk-off, breadth at dot-com lows, through negative-forward-return levels -> AI/tech pressured (OpenAI pause, Musk/Muse, MDB) offset by NVDA buyback/safety platform -> desk net seller (asset managers and hedge funds both better for sale) -> CTA RTY-futures selling projected, dealers long SPX gamma but flip short NDX above +4%.

distortions.what: Brief compresses 'the desk was a net seller, with asset managers and hedge funds both better for sale' and drops the specific activity level (3/10) and dollar amounts ($1.3bn asset managers, $1.7bn hedge funds) behind it.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the net-seller directional read is preserved; only supporting magnitude detail is omitted.

briefs.source_chain: No Middle East breakthrough pushes oil/yields higher and October hike odds above 70%, hitting high-beta/AI baskets hardest (desk views shorting Non-Profitable Tech as compelling given 7 straight months of rising 10y yields) -> GS's counter-thesis is that rates/energy/AI risks are the same but now better priced, so the pricing distribution has shifted adverse yet the asymmetry is shifting constructive -> light positioning (low sentiment, weak breadth, average valuation) helps cushion further downside -> desk flow itself was quiet, with hedge funds and long-onlys both modestly net sellers in macro products/semis and macro products/TMT respectively.
briefs.brief_chain: Same: no breakthrough -> oil/yields up, hike odds >70% -> high-beta/AI baskets sharpest decliners, short Non-Profitable Tech seen as compelling given the 7-month yield climb -> GS counter-thesis: same risks now better priced, shifting toward a more constructive asymmetry -> light positioning (sentiment, breadth, valuation) cushions declines -> quiet desk flow, HFs and LOs both net sellers in macro products/semis and macro products/TMT.

distortions.what: Brief renders the 'Paths to Relief' line as simply 'shifting the distribution of pricing toward a more constructive asymmetry,' dropping the source's own qualifier that the distribution 'shifted in a more adverse direction' before the asymmetry turned constructive.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the net conclusion (constructive asymmetry) is preserved; only an intermediate clause is compressed.

distortions.what: Brief omits the fourth 'Light Positioning' bullet (a watchlist of high-growth stocks by dispersion of analyst 3-year sales estimates).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the three positioning metrics kept (sentiment, breadth, valuation) carry the point; the dropped bullet is a supplementary watch-item, not part of the stance.

briefs.source_chain: Yields hit a two-decade high but equity vol stays near a 1-year low because the move is real-rate (not inflation) driven -> credit and oil vol widen on spreads/geopolitics while single-stock dispersion should keep rising into Q3 earnings, and Brazil's EWZ vol is richest globally ahead of its Oct 4 election -> yet SPX skew and downside-hedge demand sit near 1-year lows with ~40% of top-100 names showing inverted call skew, a bullish sentiment signal despite the rate backdrop.
briefs.brief_chain: Same overall arc, but recharacterizes the credit-vol readings (VIXIG, LQD) as 'multi-decade percentile highs' rather than the source's stated one-year percentile readings.

distortions.what: Brief states VIXIG and LQD implied vol are at 'multi-decade percentile highs.' The source's own data table labels these readings 'Percentile (1Y)' — a one-year lookback, not multi-decade — and VIXIG's reading (52nd percentile) sits barely above its one-year median, nowhere near a rare extreme. Searched 'decade' (only hit: yields' 'two-decade high,' unrelated to credit vol), '52nd percentile', '96th percentile', and 'multi-decade' (no hits) before concluding this is unsupported.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: Yes — a reader told credit vol sits at a rare multi-decade extreme would take a much higher-conviction stance (e.g., sizing up a vol-sell/fade trade) than one told it sits near an unremarkable one-year median-to-high percentile, which supports no real edge.
